Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: Original "?" resolved to 1. Table 1 (Arka 2012:152) lists 2SG ka with undergoer prefix k- on the verb. The =i absolutive clitic marks all U arguments (P and patientive S) regardless of person. While no direct ka=i example is cited, the paradigm is systematic (1SG na=i confirmed in examples 3a, 5b). Source: Arka 2012:152-153.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: Original "?" resolved to 1. Table 1 (Arka 2012:152) shows 3SG efi and 3NonSG emnde with zero undergoer prefix on verb (Ø), but the =i clitic still attaches to the U pronoun/NP itself. This is confirmed by full-NP examples such as Robertus=i, Maria=i (example 6, p.154). 3rd person U NPs take =i. Source: Arka 2012:152-154.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
curated_comment: Resolved to 1. The =i absolutive marker is not conditioned by aspect. Examples across different aspect/tense contexts show consistent =i marking on U arguments. Source: Arka 2012:153-154.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
curated_comment: Resolved to 1. Perfective examples: tamba=na Robertus=i ... feri (already=1SG Robertus=U ... give.RPST, ex.6a p.154). =i present with remote past (perfective). Source: Arka 2012:154.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
curated_comment: Resolved to 1. Multiple past-tense examples show =i on U: na=i ... kaswa=ri-ma-m (hit=1-AUX-2/3NonPL.PST, ex.5b p.154); Robertus=i ... feri (ex.6a p.154). Source: Arka 2012:153-154.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
curated_comment: Resolved to 1. Present/non-past example: daka=i taw=Ø-ramon (water=U take=3-AUX.1NonPL.PST, ex.7b p.154) and di Ø-nda-Ø (NPST, ex.7a). The =i marking is not conditioned by tense. Source: Arka 2012:154.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
curated_comment: Resolved to 1. All attested examples with =i are in the indicative mood. Source: Arka 2012:153-154.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: The patientive S of motion predicate do not receives =i, instead, receives suffix agreement.
curated_comment: Resolved to 1. The absolutive =i marking is conditioned by split intransitivity: patientive S of STATE predicates → =i (example 3a: na=i patar "I suffered from cold"); patientive S of MOTION predicates → suffix agreement instead (example 4: pa=saron-den "about to fall"); agentive S → zero. This split (verb-class-based conditioning) is the additional factor. Source: Arka 2012:153.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: Resolved to 0. There is no distinct ERGATIVE case marker in Marori. Transitive A (actor) is zero-marked; the language uses an ABSOLUTIVE marker =i (not ergative marking). Genitive/possessive uses a different marker (=na/=n for beneficiary, p.154). Source: Arka 2012:152-154.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: Resolved to 0. No distinct ergative marker exists; A is zero-marked. The instrumental is not discussed as related to the absolutive =i. Source: Arka 2012:152-154.
